headline: Bitcoin hovered near $82,000 in Asian trading after Thursday's tech-stock sell-off, as US bitcoin funds saw their first outflow of the week.

market.asOf: BTC, ETH and SOL from CoinGecko's coin pages, read 03:55 UTC 23 Oct (10:55 Bangkok). Fear & Greed read at the same time. Live prices are at the top of the page.

stories.title: Bitcoin steadies near $82,000 as the tech-stock sell-off spreads to Asia
stories.summary: Bitcoin dipped below $81,000 overnight, then climbed back toward $82,000 during Asian trading on Friday, per CoinDesk. On Thursday the Nasdaq had its worst day since June as chip stocks and Meta fell on worries about AI spending, and Asian stock markets followed lower on Friday. On Thursday crypto traded like a riskier tech stock, falling along with them.
points: At 9:30pm ET Thursday bitcoin was at $81,387, down 3.4% over 24 hours, and ether at $2,388, down 3.5%, per The Block.
Forced closures of leveraged bets: $435M in 24 hours, $385M of them bets on a rise, per CoinDesk; The Block, citing CoinGlass, puts it at $440.9M.
The Nasdaq fell 2.6% on Thursday, its worst session since June; Meta fell 6.98% and AMD 8.1%, per The Block.
In Asia on Friday the Nikkei fell 1.3% and South Korea's KOSPI 1.7%, while Brent oil touched a five-month high of $114, per Reuters via Investing.com.

stories.title: US bitcoin funds see money leave on Thursday after a strong start to the week
stories.summary: US spot bitcoin ETFs, funds that hold bitcoin for stock-market investors, took in about $1.07 billion from Monday to Wednesday. On Thursday, the day of the stock sell-off, about $381 million left, according to early SoSoValue figures reported by CoinDesk. Farside, another tracker, had not yet posted Thursday's numbers when this edition was written, so the figure may change.
points: About $381M flowed out of US spot bitcoin ETFs on Thursday, per preliminary SoSoValue data cited by CoinDesk.
Farside shows Monday +$526.7M, Tuesday +$23.2M and Wednesday +$524.8M, about $1.07B over three days.
On Wednesday BlackRock's IBIT took in $235.0M and Fidelity's FBTC $212.7M, per Farside.
Ether ETFs took in a combined $14.9M, after five straight sessions of outflows, per The Block (22 Oct).

stories.title: Washington: a Senate probe into Tether payments, and crypto rules shifting to agencies
stories.summary: Sen. Richard Blumenthal sent letters to Tether and to Nxum Group, a consulting firm co-founded by Bo Hines, the former White House crypto adviser, asking about consulting payments Tether made while Hines was advising the administration. These are questions, not findings. Separately, with the CLARITY Act market-structure bill stalled in Congress, most new US crypto rules are coming from agencies, which a future administration could change.
points: The OCC's final stablecoin rule bars issuers from paying interest directly; the American Bankers Association says it ignores "Congress's clear intent", per The Block.
JPMorgan says the CLARITY Act is unlikely to pass this year and could return in 2027, per The Block.
JPMorgan also says the current agency actions could be overturned in as soon as two years if a Democrat wins the White House, per The Block.
